Generally speaking, all visa types are issued by representation offices (→ BMEIA) abroad or, in specific exceptional cases, by certain border control posts or, where extension of the visa is permitted, by the state police headquarters.
Schengen visas must be issued by the representation office of the country in which the main travel destination of the visa applicant is located.

If the applicant intends to spend an equal amount of time in several countries (for example, when touring), the competent representation office is that of the country in whose territory the main travel destination is located, on the basis of the length and purpose of the stay.
If it is not possible to determine a main travel destination, the member country of first entry into the Schengen area is responsible for issuing the visa.
Territorial competence for applications for category A and C visas falls to the representation office in the consular district where the legal place of residence of the applicant is located.

A representation office may claim exceptional competence for applications from third‑country nationals legally residing but not registered in their district if the applicant can provide justification as to why they had to submit their application to that particular consulate.
Type D visas, however, must be applied for at the competent Austrian representation.
The provisions of Section 8 of the FPG apply to type D visas.

In accordance with these provisions, the territorial competence for carrying out official actions in relation to visas is determined on the basis of the foreign national's the place of residence (i.e.
their centre of interest, verifiable by means of e.g.
registration forms, residence permit, visa).

A list of all representation offices (addresses, telephone numbers, opening hours, special requirements for issuing visas etc.) can be found on the website of the Federal Ministry of European and International Affairs.

result.rule: Use a boolean formal conditionExpression on a conditional flow only when the description supports the condition.
Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.
Verify XML syntax, namespaces, unique IDs, reference types, scopes, and all incoming and outgoing flow references.
When the description does not justify a specialized construct, use the simplest compatible BPMN construct and do not guess missing semantics.
Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.

result.rule: When the description states a conditional clause (for example 'If ... , ...' or 'after approval ... ') that depends on the result of an earlier activity, and one outcome leads to a different path or to the end of the process: Place an exclusive gateway directly after the activity that produces the outcome. Connect that activity's completion to the gateway, and give each described outcome its own outgoing sequence flow, including the outcome that ends the process or bypasses the following activities. Do not leave the decision as an unconditional flow or omit the gateway.

When the description says a decision leads to one of two alternatives, where one alternative is a concrete action performed by a party and is followed by further described actions, or where the other alternative sends the work back so that an earlier action must be performed again: Model every described action on those branches, including the action that follows an approval or confirmation outcome and the action repeated after a return, as its own bpmn:task on the sequence flow that the description orders. Connect the return as a sequence flow back to the earlier task or gateway. Do not omit these actions, and do not replace them with a subProcess or with an end event.

When the description says a participant must perform a required action a minimum number of times (for example once per period) before the process continues, and a check follows whether the minimum has been reached: Model each required performance as a user task placed before an exclusive gateway that checks whether the minimum count has been reached. When the count is below the minimum, add a loop from the gateway back to the performing task. When the minimum is reached, add the flow that continues the process. Do not replace the repeated performances with a single task or with a timer event.

When the description lists two or more actions that must each be carried out, such as notifying different parties, without stating an order between them, and the process continues only after all of them are done: Model each such action as its own branch that starts from a parallel gateway, and join the branches with a parallel gateway before the next step. Do not use an exclusive gateway, and do not add conditions to these branches.

trace.reason: Check whether the missing preparation step before the parallel document split is already covered by an error-driven guideline.

result.rule: When the description states that one branch or outcome of a decision is followed by several separately named actions performed by different actors or departments (for example, one actor receives materials while another department sets something up), joined by 'and' or 'and also': Model each separately named action as its own task in that branch, with one task per actor action, and do not merge them into one task, even when the actions are described in the same sentence. Place the tasks in parallel after the branch's split, and join them with a parallel gateway when the description requires all of them to be completed before the process continues.

When the description lists two or more actions that must each be carried out, such as notifying different parties, without stating an order between them, and the process continues only after all of them are done: Model each such action as its own branch that starts from a parallel gateway, and join the branches with a parallel gateway before the next step. Do not use an exclusive gateway, and do not add conditions to these branches.

When the description lists several named assessments of the same item in one sentence, each with its own stated aspect (for example, one aspect, another aspect and a third aspect), and does not state their order: Model each named assessment as its own task, labeled with the assessment the description names, and do not merge them into one generic task. If the description does not order them, place them between a parallel gateway that opens the branch and a parallel gateway that closes it, so that all of them must complete before the flow continues. If the description gives an order, keep that order with sequence flows.

When the description states that, after a shared period of work, each of two parties may or must give an evaluation of the other, phrased as an action that each party performs (for example, one party can evaluate the other and the other can evaluate it back): Model each party's evaluation as its own user task performed by the party giving it, with one task per evaluation. Place these tasks in parallel after the shared period and join them with a parallel gateway before the process continues. Do not model the evaluation expected from the other party as an intermediate catch event, except where the description explicitly says the process waits for an incoming message or event.

args.text: the description states that a required item must meet a stated validity condition, such as a minimum remaining validity period or an issue-date limit, before an application can be accepted, and a later decision depends on that application

trace.reason: M1 is the only missing element the description clearly supports (passport validity and issue-date conditions in S3). I need to check whether a learned guideline already covers this validity-check task before proposing it.

result.rule: When the description states that a later decision is taken at the end of a stated period during which the process participant performs an activity, such as a leave or an absence that runs for a duration: Model the performed activity over that period as an explicit task in the flow, placed before the decision. If the period is only a passive wait with no work done, model it as a timer intermediate event instead. Do not connect the decision directly to the preceding step, so that the period appears in the model before the decision is taken.

When the description says a participant stays without performing any work until a state is reached that the description phrases as a condition becoming true, such as a position in a line being reached or an item becoming available: Model the period before that state as an intermediate catch event whose label names the awaited condition in the description's wording and present tense, placed between the step before the period and the step after it. Do not model the period as a task, because a task represents performed work and not an occurrence the flow is held for.

When the description states that an actor chooses one of two outcomes for an item they received, and the outcomes are stated as a choice the actor makes, not as a count or condition on other work: Model the choice as an exclusive gateway whose label is a question built from the decision the description states about that item. Label each outgoing flow with the outcome the description gives for that choice. Do not label the gateway with a condition on a different activity, such as a count of earlier updates or a count of recorded items, unless the description ties the choice to that condition.

When the description states that an actor may postpone a stated activity while other pending work is handled, so the activity happens only on a condition: Model the postponable activity itself as a task labeled with the activity named in the description. Place it on the branch that the stated condition selects, behind an exclusive decision gateway whose outcomes separate the postponed case from the immediate case. Do not reduce the deferral to a gateway branch that leads only to the other pending work.
